prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Managing Your Desktop Companion", "Use right-click or system tray hotkeys to dock, hide, or interact with your pet at any time.", "Right-click your pet on desktop for quick management options.", "Got It"]
2: ["Bringing Your Companion to Life", "Your companion is currently being rendered and prepared for desktop placement."]
3: ["Choose How You Want to Meet Your Companion", "Pick a pre-made pet companion or upload photos to build a custom one.", "Select Companion Path"]
4: ["Confirm desktop system tray icon is active", "Confirm & Start"]
5: ["Don't worry—you can change your companion's appearance and traits anytime after setup."]
6: ["We'll send a desktop alert as soon as your companion is ready!"]
7: ["Setup takes less than 2 minutes to complete."]
8: ["Your Companion Has Arrived on Desktop!", "Look at the bottom corner of your screen to see your active pet companion.", "Start Interacting"]
9: ["Official Companion Adoption Certificate", "Review your companion details to confirm adoption."]
